clue.text: Very easily workers are dejected

parts.note: hands are manual labourers, as in 'all hands on deck'
to be down is to be low in spirits

explanation.surface: A gloomy note that the staff are feeling low and finding things too easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are dejected' gives DOWN as in 'feeling down'.
explanation.definitionFit: To win by a wide margin without effort is an idiom for doing something with no trouble at all.

clue.text: So leap to be on the decline

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are told what they are to become, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An urge to jump while the slope runs downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' tells the solver that SO LEAP is to be turned into another word, so its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on a slant that slopes downward is literally on the decline.

clue.text: Delicacy coming out of a tin within 24 hours

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the word for a day

parts.note: a day lasts twenty-four hours

indicators.note: letters coming out of a container emerge jumbled, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A tasty treat emerges from a tin inside a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' rearranges A TIN into AINT, and 'within' puts that inside DAY. The printed text seems to have dropped the 'a' the anagram needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dainty is a small choice morsel, a treat or titbit.

clue.text: Double dagger that is found in Diss, strangely enough

indicators.note: found in puts the abbreviation for that is among the letters of the town's name
strangely suggests the combined letters are set out in an odd new order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A printer's mark turns up, oddly, in a Norfolk market town.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small town in Norfolk, England. 'found in' puts IE inside DISS, and 'strangely enough' rearranges the result.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing the double dagger symbol is also called a diesis, a reference mark for footnotes.

clue.text: An elementary prognostication

parts.note: elementary is read as about the elements, wind and rain, so this is a prediction of the elements

explanation.definitionFit: A forecast of rain, sun and wind is a prediction about the elements.

clue.text: Instrumentalist on the beach might take flight

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on top of the other comes first

parts.note: a beach is a stretch of sand
a piper plays the bagpipes or pipe

explanation.surface: A bagpiper playing on the shore might run off.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts PIPER below SAND. The definition is cryptic: a bird is something that might take flight.
explanation.definitionFit: This shore-dwelling wading bird is something that can fly away.

clue.text: Set to stare at an evergreen shrub

parts.note: to goggle is to stare wide-eyed
box is a hedging evergreen shrub

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stare at a hedge plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' means a television set; GOGGLE-BOX is British slang for a television.
explanation.definitionFit: A goggle-box is informal British slang for a television receiver.

clue.text: Norma made other notes

indicators.note: an other version of the letters means a different arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A woman named Norma wrote some more notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' asks for NORMA MADE in another order.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda is the Latin plural of memorandum, written reminders or messages.

clue.text: Convict returns raw material in abundance

indicators.note: returns means the word for convict is read backwards

parts.note: an old lag is a habitual convict
ore is the raw rock from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: A prisoner comes back with plenty of raw goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns LAG into GAL, then ORE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty, aplenty: the word follows its noun, as in prizes in great quantity.

clue.text: Stingy with lira I'll be exchanging

indicators.note: exchanging places of letters shuffles them, as currency is exchanged

explanation.surface: Someone mean with money while changing Italian currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanging' rearranges LIRA, I'LL and BE; the lira was Italy's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiberal can mean ungenerous, mean with money, the opposite of liberal giving.

clue.text: I go round after the girl slowly

indicators.note: after places the rearranged pair behind the girl's name

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name

indicators.note: turning letters round reorders them, here the two words before it

explanation.surface: Someone goes round chasing a young woman at a slow pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges I GO into GIO, and 'after' puts that behind ADA.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical tempo marking meaning at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Draw attention to the stage illumination

explanation.definitionFit: To highlight is to draw attention; a theatre lamp beams a bright circle on an actor.

clue.text: Came in dishevelled for entertainment

indicators.note: dishevelled means messed up, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone arrived scruffy for a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishevelled' rearranges CAME IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the pictures is a form of amusement for an evening out.

clue.text: Unusually fine story, too overwhelming to be expressed in words

definitions.text: too overwhelming to be expressed in words

indicators.note: unusually signals the next word is set in an unusual order

parts.note: a fable is a short moral tale

explanation.surface: A remarkably good tale leaves one speechless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges FINE into INEF, followed by FABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond description cannot be uttered; it is unspeakable.

clue.text: Ascribe a characteristic quality

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to credit something to a cause; as a noun it is a typical trait or feature.

clue.text: Forthright, like soap-box orator?

explanation.definitionFit: Candid and blunt in speech; a soap-box orator also speaks his mind out in the open air.

clue.text: Bachelor accepts redhead's undergarment

indicators.note: accepts means the degree letters take another letter inside them

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
the head of the word red is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: A single man takes delivery of a red-haired woman's lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts R, the head of 'red', inside BA.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is an item of women's underwear.

clue.text: Window at the front of the ship?

explanation.definitionFit: A curved bay window is called a bow window; the forward end of a vessel is its bow.

clue.text: A note for the goddess

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A message left for a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' means a musical note, TE from do-re-mi, not a written message. Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Ate is the deity of folly and rash action.

clue.text: Still in danger in the 21

explanation.walkthrough: 'the 21' points to the answer at 21, the wooded area: anyone in the trees has not yet got clear of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means not yet free of difficulties; literally, someone still among the trees.

clue.text: Grief is said to stop a horse

indicators.note: is said means the word is spoken, giving its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: whoa is the call a rider gives to halt a horse

explanation.surface: A rider's call to halt a mount is described as sorrowful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is said' gives the sound of WHOA, the rider's call, spelt WOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Woe is deep sorrow or distress.

clue.text: Anticipate everybody leaving the wooded area

indicators.note: leaving means the word for everybody departs from the longer word

parts.note: to forestall is to act ahead of, to anticipate
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Predicting that everyone will quit the woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes ALL from FORESTALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tract of land covered with trees is a woodland.

clue.text: It is clear Lulu loses half the money

indicators.note: losing half the name leaves only its first two letters

parts.note: a cent is a coin, a unit of money

explanation.surface: Lulu is clearly short of half her cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses half' keeps LU from LULU; CENT follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucent means shining or translucent, letting light through.

clue.text: Percival lumbered partly by an old earthwork

indicators.note: partly means only part of these words is used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Percival clumped along beside an ancient rampart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' points to the letters running across PerciVAL LUMbered.
explanation.definitionFit: A vallum is a Roman rampart or defensive ditch, like the one beside Hadrian's Wall.

clue.text: It doesn't sound as if one is able to get the bird

definitions.text: It doesn't sound as if one is able to get the bird

parts.words: It doesn't sound as if one is able to get the bird
parts.note: the bird's name sounds like a pair being able, not a single one

explanation.definitionFit: This tropical bird with a huge bill has a name that sounds like two being capable.

clue.text: Controlling device to be in, eluded at frequent intervals

indicators.note: included means the short word goes inside the longer one

parts.note: something regular happens at frequent, even intervals

explanation.surface: A control gadget needs to be fitted often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts TO inside REGULAR; the printed text broke the word into 'in, eluded'.
explanation.definitionFit: A regulator is a mechanism that governs flow or speed, like a thermostat.

clue.text: West Bromwich, a team of Rovers in Scotland!

definitions.text: a team of Rovers in Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: West Bromwich Albion is an English football club; Albion Rovers is a Scottish one.
explanation.definitionFit: Both football clubs share the old poetic name for Britain in their titles.

clue.text: Happen to finish in the first three

definitions.text: to finish in the first three

explanation.definitionFit: To occur; and in racing a horse that is 'placed' finishes second or third, so it takes a podium position.

clue.text: Untidy young animals

explanation.definitionFit: Scattered rubbish makes a place messy; a brood of puppies or kittens born together is a litter.

clue.text: New Testament account

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A fresh version of the Bible's second part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges TESTAMENT; the surface points to the New Testament of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is a report or record, such as a bank account summary.
